runs.content: Friday focus domains (Lightfin, Games, Cooking, Sports Betting, Work) had no fresh wiki activity since the 2026-08-27 catch-up run — log.md shows no new entries touching any of the five between then and today, aside from a skipped recipe-recommender run (no duplicate suggestions generated). Checked every live angle in these domains against the existing open list in wiki/cross-domain-themes.md: Games' four prototype stubs are still an unpopulated placeholder table, Games Workshop (GAW.L) still has no dedicated Finance idea page despite the +300% pension gain flagged as a hedging candidate three weeks ago, Workday (WDAY) still hasn't been added to Finance's short-research Watch List despite idea-wday.md's own Bear Case laying out exactly the red flags the tracker looks for, and Sports Betting's Bookmakers table is still a single placeholder row unchanged since May despite Burry's DraftKings/Flutter "anti-prediction-markets" thesis being logged as relevant three weeks ago. All four were already open items — nothing has moved on any of them, and no new angle surfaced. Per the task's own quality bar (a quiet day shouldn't be padded with filler), zero new investigation ideas or cross-domain connections were logged today; the cross-domain-themes.md frontmatter date was bumped to reflect the run.

**Investigation idea:** A fully-written, substantial podcast page is missing from the master catalog entirely, even though it's cited as a live source from a Finance model. podcasts/podcast-dwarkesh-compute-prices-10x.md ("Why Smarter AI Models Could Drive Up Compute Prices 10x," updated 2026-08-04, Status: Completed — listened) is one of the more developed podcast pages in the wiki: Patel's GPU-rental-pricing thesis in full, plus an explicit three-way reconciliation against Benedict Evans's commoditisation view and Michael Burry's circular-financing critique. It's correctly listed in podcasts/podcast-list.md, and finance/models/model-hyperscaler-gpu-token-debt-2026-08-05.md's own See Also section cites it directly as a source the model tests against. But a grep of wiki/index.md's Podcasts table for "compute-prices" or "10x" returns nothing — the page simply isn't there, unlike every other podcast page created around the same date. Same class of gap already flagged for Cooking and Books pages in prior runs. Next step: add a row for podcast-dwarkesh-compute-prices-10x.md to wiki/index.md's Podcasts section.

**Cross-domain connection:** Michael Lewis's own origin-story book on the birth of the mortgage-bond market is sitting unlinked from Finance's own mapping of how AI data-centre debt hides in a structurally identical vehicle four decades later. books/book-liars-poker.md documents Salomon Brothers inventing the mortgage-backed security in the 1980s; the page's own Why Notable section calls it "directly continuous with the collapse [Lewis] later covered in The Big Short." finance/models/model-hyperscaler-gpu-token-debt-2026-08-05.md's Section 4 maps, in comparable structural detail, how ~$1.65 trillion of AI data-centre debt is kept off hyperscaler balance sheets via SPV/JV vehicles (Meta's Hyperion, Oracle/OpenAI's Abilene SPV) funded by private credit that traces through to PE-owned life insurers' policyholder capital, with state guaranty funds as the final backstop — a chain its own cited source (TFTC) explicitly frames as an "Enron comparison." Both describe the same underlying pattern: an industry inventing a structuring vehicle that lets debt/risk be created and sold without appearing where investors would naturally look for it, praised as financial engineering right up until it isn't. book-liars-poker.md's Why Notable section stops at "foreshadowing the 2008 crisis" without noting the pattern has already repeated in a domain Fred is actively researching today. Neither page cites the other. Next step: add a line to book-liars-poker.md's Why Notable section citing the AI-debt-structuring model as a live, current-day instance of the same off-book risk-shifting mechanism the book first documented, cross-linked both ways.

Thursday focus (Books + Podcasts): the wiki had a 17-day gap with no scheduled-task activity between the 2026-08-10 run and today (laptop off), so no new Books/Podcasts content existed to deep-dive — today's email-to-clipping run (8 emails, unsorted) was the only intervening wiki activity. With nothing fresh to synthesize, this run instead audited existing Books/Podcasts pages against the whole-wiki map for connections the 17-day gap hadn't surfaced yet, and found one indexing gap plus one genuinely new thematic pairing rather than padding with weaker material. No items resolved this run.
